subtopics.title: Training Needs Analysis
learningObjectives: Explain the purpose of a training needs analysis.
Identify factors that can indicate a need for worker training.
Distinguish training needs from problems that require other controls.

data.content: Training needs analysis is a systematic process used to identify gaps between the knowledge, skills, competencies, and qualifications required for safe and effective work and those currently demonstrated by workers.
The results help determine whether training is required and what type of training should be provided.

mainContent.title: Why Training Needs Analysis is Important

data.content: A structured assessment helps an organization identify actual competence requirements instead of assuming that a worker needs training.
Training should address an identified competence or performance need. Not every performance problem is solved by training.

data.title: Workplace Example
data.content: An assessment identifies that workers are required to perform a task involving a specific operating procedure, but several workers cannot demonstrate the required procedure correctly. The competence gap may indicate a need for additional training and assessment.
Incident trends, audit findings, observations, assessment results, changes in work processes, and supervisor feedback can provide information that helps identify potential training needs.

mainContent.title: When Training May Not Be the Correct Solution

data.title: Important
data.content: A performance problem does not automatically mean that training is required. The underlying cause should be identified before selecting training as a control.
Identify the cause of the performance gap before deciding that training is the solution.

keyPoints.title: Key Point 1
keyPoints.content: Training needs should be identified systematically.

keyPoints.title: Key Point 2
keyPoints.content: Competence requirements should be clearly understood.

keyPoints.title: Key Point 3
keyPoints.content: Performance information can help identify potential training needs.

keyPoints.title: Key Point 4
keyPoints.content: Training should not automatically be selected as the solution to every performance problem.

data.content: A worker is unable to demonstrate a required safety procedure during an assessment. Further training may be required before the worker is considered competent.

A company observes repeated errors during a routine task. Before arranging additional training, the organization investigates whether the problem is related to worker knowledge and skills, unclear procedures, equipment limitations, supervision, or another underlying factor.
A proper needs assessment helps determine whether training is actually required.

examTips.title: Training is not always the solution
examTips.content: When a question describes a performance problem, consider whether the underlying cause has been identified before selecting training as the solution.

commonMistakes.title: Assuming training is always required
commonMistakes.content: Assuming that every performance problem is caused by a lack of training.

keyTakeaways.title: Takeaway 1
keyTakeaways.content: Training needs analysis identifies gaps between required and demonstrated competence.

keyTakeaways.title: Takeaway 2
keyTakeaways.content: Evidence should be used to identify potential training needs.

keyTakeaways.title: Takeaway 3
keyTakeaways.content: The underlying cause of a performance problem should be considered before selecting training.
